newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pangestu says no plan to sell Astra stake.
newsitem.headline: Pangestu says no plan to sell Astra stake.

text.p: Indonesian timber tycoon Prajogo Pangestu said on Monday that he had no plans to sell his 10.68 percent stake in the country's biggest automobile manufacturer Astra International.
"At the moment, I have no plans to sell my Astra shares," Pangestu told reporters, adding that he had not been approached with any offer for the holding.
Pangestu's Delta Mustika company owns 10.68 percent in Astra, one of the largest individual holdings in the car firm.
Two groups with close links to President Suharto, the Nusamba group and the Salim group, bought sizeable chunks in Astra last week, brokers said.
Nusamba, headed by magnate Muhamad "Bob" Hasan, is 80 percent owned by three charitable foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan and the president's eldest son Sigit Hardjojudanto own 10 percent each.
The Salim group is controlled by Liem Sioe Liong, believed to be Indonesia's richest man and a close associate of Suharto.
Brokers have said their holdings in Astra could total up to 30 percent of the company. But they said the stakes could be held by various companies in the two groups.
